name: Dungeons & Dragons
tagline: Collaborative storytelling in a world of infinite possibility
description: Dungeons & Dragons (D&D) is the world's best-known tabletop roleplaying game. One player acts as the Dungeon Master (DM), narrating a fantasy world, while others create characters and collaboratively tell an epic story. The 5th edition is the most accessible version yet.

guide.objective: Work together as a group of adventurers to overcome challenges, explore the world, and tell a compelling story — there's no single winner.
quickRules: One player is the Dungeon Master (DM) — they run the world and all NPCs
Other players create and control characters (Player Characters / PCs)
Roll a d20 + modifiers to resolve uncertain actions (Ability Checks)
Combat is turn-based with structured Initiative order
Characters gain experience and level up through adventure

sections.title: The Core Mechanic
sections.content: Almost everything in D&D 5e resolves with one core mechanic: roll a d20, add a relevant modifier, compare to a Difficulty Class (DC).

diagram.caption: The D&D dice set — d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20, d100

rules.title: The d20 Roll
rules.description: Roll a 20-sided die (d20). Add your relevant ability modifier (Strength, Dexterity, etc.) and any proficiency bonus if applicable.

rules.title: Difficulty Class (DC)
rules.description: The DM sets a target number (DC) for tasks. Roll equal to or higher to succeed. Easy tasks might be DC 10; nearly impossible feats might be DC 25.

rules.title: Advantage & Disadvantage
rules.description: Advantage: roll two d20s, keep the higher. Disadvantage: roll two d20s, keep the lower. These reflect favorable or unfavorable circumstances.

rules.title: Critical Hit (Natural 20)
rules.description: Rolling a 20 on the die (before modifiers) in combat is a critical hit — you deal double damage dice. Rolling a 1 is a critical miss — your attack automatically fails.

rules.title: Six Ability Scores
rules.description: Every character has 6 scores: Strength (STR), Dexterity (DEX), Constitution (CON), Intelligence (INT), Wisdom (WIS), Charisma (CHA). Scores typically range from 8–18 at character creation.

rules.title: Ability Modifiers
rules.description: Each score converts to a modifier: score 10–11 = +0, 12–13 = +1, 14–15 = +2, 16–17 = +3, 18 = +4. Modifiers are added to relevant rolls.

rules.title: Race & Class
rules.description: Choose a race (Human, Elf, Dwarf, etc.) that grants ability bonuses and traits. Choose a class (Fighter, Wizard, Rogue, etc.) that defines your abilities, Hit Points, and skills.

rules.title: Hit Points (HP)
rules.description: HP represents how much damage your character can take. When HP reaches 0, you're unconscious. At 0 HP you make Death Saving Throws — three failures means death.

steps.title: Determine Surprise
steps.description: If one side ambushes the other, the surprised party cannot act during the first round of combat.

steps.title: Roll Initiative
steps.description: Everyone rolls d20 + DEX modifier. This determines turn order — highest goes first. The DM rolls for monsters (often as a group).
steps.tip: Write down the initiative order and post it visibly — it speeds up combat enormously.

steps.title: Take Your Turn
steps.description: On your turn you get: 1 Action (attack, cast a spell, dash, etc.), 1 Bonus Action (if a feature gives it), movement up to your speed, and 1 free object interaction.

steps.title: Attack Roll
steps.description: Roll d20 + attack modifier vs. the target's Armor Class (AC). If your result meets or beats the AC, you hit — then roll damage dice.
steps.tip: Melee attacks use STR modifier; ranged and finesse attacks may use DEX.

rules.title: Spell Slots
rules.description: Spellcasters have a limited number of 'spell slots' per rest. Casting a spell expends a slot. You regain all slots after a Long Rest (8 hours).

rules.title: Spell Levels
rules.description: Spells range from cantrips (level 0, unlimited uses) to 9th-level spells (the most powerful). Higher-slot casting of lower-level spells often improves their effect.

rules.title: Concentration
rules.description: Some spells require concentration to maintain their effect. You can only concentrate on one spell at a time; taking damage may break concentration (CON saving throw, DC = 10 or half damage taken).

variants.name: One-Shot Adventures
variants.description: A self-contained adventure completed in a single session (3–5 hours). Great for introducing new players to D&D.

variants.name: West Marches Campaign
variants.description: A large sandbox setting where different groups of players explore the same world in separate sessions — perfect for large groups with scheduling constraints.

tips.title: Focus on fun, not optimization
tips.content: Your first character doesn't need to be mechanically perfect. Pick a concept that excites you — a grumpy dwarf baker who became an adventurer, or a curious wizard who collects odd hats. The story matters more than the stats.

tips.title: Session Zero is essential
tips.content: Before campaign play, hold a 'Session Zero' — discuss tone, themes, boundaries (content X-Card), character backstories, and player expectations. This prevents most future table conflicts.

tips.title: Communicate with your party
tips.content: D&D is cooperative. Talk strategy openly, coordinate spells and abilities, and support each other's characters. A well-coordinated party beats a group of lone wolves every time.

tips.title: Learn the action economy
tips.content: Combat in D&D is about maximizing what you can accomplish in your action, bonus action, and movement. Classes and features that grant extra actions or bonus actions are disproportionately powerful.
